chunks: Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that he said:

There are five who do not sleep: one distressed over blood he is to shed, the possessor of abundant wealth who has no trustworthy keeper, one who speaks falsehood and slander among people for a worldly gain he attains, one encumbered with much wealth while having no wealth himself, and one who loves a beloved and anticipates separation from him.

key_terms.الْبُهْتَانَ: Slander or false accusation against others.
key_terms.الْهَامُّ: One who is distressed, anxious, or preoccupied.
key_terms.بِدَمٍ: With blood; referring to unlawful killing or bloodshed.
key_terms.خَمْسَةٌ: Five categories of people mentioned in the hadith.
key_terms.عَرَضٍ: A fleeting worldly gain or temporary benefit.
key_terms.فِرَاقَهُ: His separation; parting from a beloved person.

ai.seo_question: Which kinds of people are described in the hadith as being unable to sleep, and why?
ai.summary: This hadith identifies five kinds of people whose inner states deprive them of sleep, highlighting the unrest caused by guilt, mistrust, greed, burden, and fear of separation. It serves as an ethical teaching about the psychological consequences of wrongdoing, attachment, and worldly anxiety.
